steps.intent: The United Kingdom’s objectives are to renew AUSSOM’s mandate, preserve Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, strengthen counter-terrorism and protection of civilians, and move towards predictable financing under resolution 2719. The most difficult points will be the financing language, because several members remain cautious about UN-assessed contributions; the balance between FGS consent and AU troop-contributor arrangements; and language on FGS–FMS cooperation, compliance and human rights that must be firm enough for the UK but acceptable to all veto holders.

messages.Algeria: We thank the penholder and support the renewal of AUSSOM, but OP7 must not defer the key financing decision. As we have consistently stated with the A3+, AUSSOM should be financed through the hybrid implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), with predictable, sustainable and flexible resources, including assessed contributions and an AU token contribution. We also ask that PP13 explicitly reaffirm Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity and call on regional States to refrain from unilateral actions that undermine them.
messages.China: China supports the timely renewal of AUSSOM to preserve counter-terrorism gains and avoid a security vacuum. We request that OP7 make financing under resolution 2719 more operational and that OP5 refer specifically to resolution 2714 (2023) and to diversion to Al-Shabaab, so as not to constrain Somali security forces. We also suggest balanced regional language on the sovereignty of all States in the region.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of AUSSOM and welcomes the UK penhold. We would like the text to strengthen humanitarian access, women's participation, child protection and climate-related reporting, all of which are central to Denmark's approach. We can accept the draft as a basis, but these changes should be reflected before the vote.
messages.France: France welcomes the United Kingdom's draft and supports the renewal of AUSSOM. We ask that the financing paragraph be strengthened to reflect resolution 2719 (2023), burden-sharing and the continued engagement of the European Union and new partners, and that the compliance framework explicitly include the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We also seek clearer reporting on conditions-based benchmarks for the progressive transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of AUSSOM and the conditions-based approach in the draft. We ask that OP2(a) explicitly include countering piracy and armed robbery at sea, reflecting our long-standing maritime security interest and experience in Operation Atalanta. We also seek stronger language on respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and on civilian harm mitigation in OP3.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the timely renewal of AUSSOM and the Council’s continued focus on Somali ownership, sovereignty and security. We propose strengthening the humanitarian access language with the humanitarian principles, adding concrete climate risk and climate finance support, and reaffirming accountability and the full participation of women and youth in elections. These changes would reinforce the protection and prevention objectives of the mandate.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of AUSSOM and welcomes the UK draft as a good basis. We ask the penholder to strengthen language on Somalia’s sovereignty, unity and non-interference, to add explicit provision for TCC/PCC consultations, and to reinforce predictable financing under resolution 2719, including consideration of UN assessed contributions. We are ready to engage constructively to refine these points.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of AUSSOM and welcomes the draft’s focus on sovereignty, humanitarian access and protection of civilians. We would like OP7 to signal a clearer path to predictable financing under resolution 2719 (2023), and we propose an operative call on all States to respect Somalia’s sovereignty and resolve regional disputes peacefully. These changes would strengthen the Council’s support for an African Union-led mission that is sustainable and accountable to the whole membership.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the timely renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and the draft’s conditions-based approach to security transition. We would like the text to reflect more explicitly the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy in AUSSOM’s compliance framework, consistent with our prior emphasis on conduct and human rights compliance. On financing, we welcome OP7 but believe it should be more decision-oriented so that the Council can consider the resolution 2719 modalities by 31 May 2026, giving AUSSOM predictable and sustainable support. We can support the draft with these adjustments.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the timely renewal of AUSSOM. Our amendments are aimed at strengthening host-country consent and Somali sovereignty, preserving the General Assembly's budgetary prerogatives under resolution 2719 (2023), and ensuring that references to climate and local procurement are balanced and consistent with Council practice. We look forward to the penholder taking these concerns on board so that the Council can act unitedly.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the United Kingdom for the draft and supports the renewal of AUSSOM. We ask that OP7 move beyond 'options' to concrete modalities for applying resolution 2719, including assessed contributions, so that AUSSOM has predictable and sustainable financing. We also seek explicit T/PCC consultation in OP6 and a clear operational call in OP4 on all regional States to respect Somalia's sovereignty and resolve disputes peacefully.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the timely renewal of AUSSOM and thanks the United Kingdom for the draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP7 so that predictable and sustainable financing under resolution 2719 is not deferred again, and to make human rights compliance and the women, peace and security agenda more operational in the mandate. These changes are important for Slovenia’s support and reflect our consistent position on AUSSOM’s effectiveness and credibility.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the timely renewal of AUSSOM and thanks the penholder for the balanced draft. We ask the Council to strengthen OP7 so that resolution 2719 modalities, including access to assessed contributions of up to 75 per cent, are applied now rather than deferred, and to make clear in OP1 that AUSSOM's troop and police contributions are determined with the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia. We also seek technical corrections to OP5 to ensure the arms embargo targets Al-Shabaab and other non-State armed groups, not Somalia's sovereign security forces.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewing AUSSOM to counter Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da'esh, but we cannot accept automatic or implied UN assessed contributions. We need OP7 to make any assessed contributions subject to a separate Council decision, with the African Union meeting its 25 per cent share, and we want clearer conditions-based benchmarks and reporting. We can support the text with these changes.

steps.summary: The revision broadens consensus by incorporating humanitarian, women, peace and security, regional sovereignty, TCC/PCC consultation and review provisions. It preserves the penholder's core financing compromise: no automatic United Nations assessed contributions, but a costed proposal and a separate Council decision with a clear decision horizon. The draft should secure adoption without a P5 veto, though Algeria, Slovenia and Somalia may abstain on financing.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of AUSSOM and welcomes the inclusion of language on Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. However, the financing paragraph remains too open-ended: we need an earlier costed proposal and a clear commitment to decide on 2719 modalities promptly, with assessed contributions considered in accordance with Council procedures. We also ask that OP1 avoid ambiguous references to bilateral agreements that could undermine Somali consent and sovereignty.
messages.China: China supports the revised text and welcomes the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier comments on resolution 2714 (2023), regional sovereignty and possible assessed contributions. To make the financing language operational and predictable, we ask that OP11 explicitly link AUSSOM financing to accelerated implementation of the Joint AU–UN Roadmap under resolution 2719 (2023), with any assessed contributions subject to a separate Council decision and full respect for General Assembly budgetary procedures. China can join consensus on this basis.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes the revised text, which now reflects our priorities on humanitarian access and principles, child protection, women’s full and meaningful participation, climate-related security reporting and regional respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The draft provides a robust, conditions-based framework for AUSSOM’s renewal and for the progressive transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. We thank the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests and support the text as it stands.
messages.France: France supports the revised text and is ready to vote in favour. We welcome that our priorities on the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, conditions-based transfer benchmarks, burden-sharing and EU engagement are reflected, and that any use of assessed contributions remains subject to a separate Council decision and respect for the budgetary prerogatives of the General Assembly. France encourages the Council to adopt the resolution swiftly ahead of the expiry of AUSSOM’s mandate.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the current draft and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier concerns on maritime security, civilian harm mitigation and sovereignty/dialogue. The text provides a timely, conditions-based renewal of AUSSOM and reflects the importance of predictable financing, protection of civilians and respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Greece will vote in favour and encourages all members to unite behind the resolution.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the current text as revised and has no further changes to request. We appreciate the penholder’s incorporation of humanitarian principles, climate risk and climate finance, women and youth participation, and accountability language. We encourage the Council to unite behind the renewal of AUSSOM and to ensure timely, predictable support for its implementation.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the revised draft. We welcome the inclusion of language on Somalia’s sovereignty, unity and non-interference, and on systematic TCC/PCC consultation. We also accept the financing paragraph as a balanced compromise that preserves the modalities of resolution 2719 and the prerogatives of the General Assembly, and we will vote in favour.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder for incorporating the 90-day horizon for a financing decision and the operative call on regional States to respect Somalia's sovereignty and resolve disputes peacefully. The text as drafted appropriately supports AUSSOM's mandate, conditions-based transfer, humanitarian access, compliance with international law and predictable financing under resolution 2719 while respecting the General Assembly's budgetary prerogatives. Panama therefore supports the current text and will vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the inclusion of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy and the strengthened troop- and police-contributing country consultation language, and is prepared to support the draft. We continue to believe that predictable financing for AUSSOM requires a fixed Council decision date; we therefore ask the penholder to replace the 90-day horizon in OP11 with a decision by 31 May 2026, as previously proposed. This would allow the Council to act promptly following the 31 March costed proposal and keep implementation of resolution 2719 on track.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the current draft as a balanced basis for renewing AUSSOM. We welcome the incorporation of the Federal Government of Somalia's request and consent, the reference to Somali law and the Constitution for elections, the protection of the General Assembly's budgetary prerogatives, and local procurement. We note that the climate wording retains a reference to climate change, but this is not a blocker. We are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of AUSSOM and welcomes the incorporation of TCC/PCC consultation and regional sovereignty language. We still believe OP11 should move from options to concrete modalities for applying resolution 2719, including assessed contributions subject to a separate Council decision, so that the AU and troop contributors have predictable financing. We also ask that the strategic review in OP3 explicitly consult TCCs and PCCs. We are ready to support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the inclusion of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, civilian harm mitigation, women's participation and strengthened reporting, and remains ready to support the renewal of AUSSOM. Our remaining priority is OP11: financing must be predictable, sustainable and adequate, and resolution 2719 (2023) must be implemented fully and in a timely manner. The current open-ended timeline risks prolonging uncertainty, so we ask for the OP11 additions above and can support the text once they are reflected.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the revised text and appreciates the correction in OP9 and the recognition of FGS consent in OP1. However, OP1 must explicitly confirm that AUSSOM's troop- and police-contributing countries and overall composition are determined with the Federal Government of Somalia's consent, consistent with our bilateral agreements. On financing, Somalia continues to seek predictable support through resolution 2719, including assessed contributions up to 75 per cent, and asks the penholder to reflect that priority in OP11.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised text and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of our financing red line and the strategic review with benchmarks. We still seek two adjustments: maintaining 90-day reporting to ensure robust Council oversight, and removing references to climate change and climate finance in OP12 in line with our policy. With those changes, we are prepared to vote in favour.

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

replies.Algeria: accepted: OP11 now sets a 31 January 2026 costed proposal, concrete modalities and a 60-day financing decision; OP1 consent language clarified.
replies.China: accepted: OP11 links financing to accelerated Roadmap implementation and assessed contributions subject to a separate Council decision.
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: OP11 now sets a financing decision by 31 May 2026.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: OP11 uses concrete modalities; OP3 adds TCC/PCC consultation.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: OP11 adds full and timely implementation, adequate financing, and a fixed 31 May 2026 decision date.
replies.Somalia: partially accepted: OP1 adds FGS consent over AUSSOM composition; OP11 recognizes potential assessed contributions but does not grant automatic 75 per cent access.
replies.United States of America: accepted: OP13 now requires 90-day reporting; OP12 removes climate change and climate finance references.

steps.summary: The revised text accommodates key financing, sovereignty, TCC/PCC consultation and US reporting/climate requests. It preserves the requirement for a separate Council decision on assessed contributions, so Somalia is expected to abstain while all P5 members and at least nine others vote in favour.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s priority was predictable financing and explicit respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and consent; the revised text accommodates both, so Algeria supports the renewal.
reasons.China: China supports the renewal of AUSSOM and its key financing concern was accepted by the penholder. Voting in favour is consistent with China’s emphasis on Somali sovereignty, African Union ownership, and predictable AU-led peace support operations.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported the draft in negotiations and has no requested changes; it aligns with Denmark’s priorities on sovereignty, humanitarian access, human rights, WPS and predictable peace-operation financing. Denmark therefore votes yes.
reasons.France: France consistently supports AUSSOM renewal and had already signalled support without requested changes; the draft aligns with French priorities on counterterrorism, Somali sovereignty, humanitarian access, and sustainable financing under resolution 2719.
reasons.Greece: Greece had already indicated support with no requested changes and consistently backs AU-led peace support, Somali sovereignty, humanitarian access and compliance. The draft aligns with those priorities, so Greece votes in favour.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported Somalia-related resolutions, raised no changes, and prioritizes Somalia’s sovereignty, AU-led peace support, humanitarian law, and women’s participation, making a yes vote with a supportive explanation appropriate.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported Somalia’s stability, sovereignty and African Union-led peace operations, and the draft is balanced, renewal-focused and responsive to Pakistan’s priorities on T/PCC consultation and predictable financing. It therefore votes yes.
reasons.Panama: Panama’s last-round position was support and it has consistently favoured multilateral support for Somali peace and security, provided international law and sovereignty are upheld. The draft aligns with those priorities, so Panama votes in favour and explains its vote.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported AUSSOM and the Council’s consensus on Somalia; the accepted OP11 change addresses its key financing-timeline concern. Voting in favour aligns with its support for peacekeeping continuity, counterterrorism, and predictable financing.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation had already signalled support and the draft preserves Somali sovereignty, African Union ownership, and conditions further financing decisions on separate Council and General Assembly action. No Russian red lines are crossed, so Moscow would vote in favour without needing an explanation before the vote.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supported the renewal of AUSSOM and its key requested amendments on financing modalities and troop/police-contributing country consultation were accepted. There was no need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Slovenia: The penholder accepted Slovenia’s red-line request on OP11, and the draft aligns with Slovenia’s established support for AUSSOM, civilian protection, human rights compliance, women’s participation, and predictable financing.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia’s red line on Federal Government consent over AUSSOM’s composition is reflected in OP1. Although the financing text falls short of Somalia’s preferred automatic access to up to 75 per cent assessed contributions, rejecting or abstaining on a mandate renewal that protects Somali sovereignty and keeps AUSSOM in place would be counterproductive.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is the penholder and has consistently supported AUSSOM renewals, Somali sovereignty, counterterrorism, humanitarian access, and resolution 2719 financing, so it votes in favour and explains its vote before adoption.
reasons.United States of America: The draft accommodates the United States’ key requested reporting change, preserves strong counterterrorism and compliance provisions, and advances U.S. support for AUSSOM while safeguarding budgetary and financing considerations. The United States would vote in favour and explain its support, including on financing, sovereignty, and burden-sharing.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that the penholder has taken on board key concerns of the A3+ regarding predictable, sustainable and flexible financing for AUSSOM, including a concrete timeline for the joint costed proposal and a 60-day decision on financing modalities in line with resolution 2719 (2023). We also welcome the reaffirmation of the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia, and the clarification that the composition of AUSSOM shall be determined in close coordination with and with the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia. We stress that the AU-led character of the mission, full respect for Somali ownership, and non-interference in Somalia’s internal affairs remain essential. We call on all partners to ensure adequate and predictable support for AUSSOM and for the Somali security forces, and we urge all States in the region to resolve their disputes peacefully and in full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
before.China: China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate to help Somalia counter terrorism, protect civilians and build its security capacity, in full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and ownership. We welcome the incorporation of China’s proposal on financing, which links AUSSOM’s funding to accelerated implementation of resolution 2719 (2023) and the Joint African Union–United Nations Roadmap, while preserving the budgetary prerogatives of the General Assembly. China hopes that the African Union, Somalia and all partners will ensure a conditions-based transition, avoid a security vacuum, and provide predictable and sustainable support. We call on all parties to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel and to advance reconciliation and national priorities.
before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and the conditions-based approach to the progressive transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. We underline the importance of full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability under international humanitarian and human rights law, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace and security efforts. We also stress the need for predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM while respecting the budgetary prerogatives of the General Assembly.
before.France: France thanks the United Kingdom for its work and will vote in favour of this resolution. Renewing AUSSOM is essential to prevent a security vacuum and to support Somali forces in the fight against Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh; France reaffirms its full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and calls on all States in the region to refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine it. We also stress the centrality of protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. On financing, France supports predictable, sustainable and flexible support in line with resolution 2719 (2023), including burden-sharing among all partners and continued engagement by the European Union. Only a coordinated response by all of Somalia’s partners can effectively stem the terrorist threat.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and its role in helping Somalia counter Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates, protect civilians and facilitate humanitarian access. We reaffirm full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and stress the importance of a conditions-based transfer of security responsibilities, compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law, the full and meaningful participation of women, and predictable financing for African Union-led peace support operations in line with resolution 2719 (2023) and the prerogatives of the General Assembly.
before.Guyana: Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and the clear reaffirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity. We underscore that international support must remain grounded in the consent and priorities of the Federal Government of Somalia, with close coordination with federal member states and troop- and police-contributing countries. Guyana also stresses the importance of predictable and sustainable financing for African Union-led peace support operations, full respect for international humanitarian and human rights law, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace and security efforts.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan votes in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate in full respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and in accordance with the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia. Pakistan commends the African Union and troop- and police-contributing countries for their sacrifices and stresses the need for systematic consultation with contributing countries, predictable and sustainable financing under resolution 2719 (2023), and continued attention to the protection of civilians, humanitarian access and a conditions-based transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces.
before.Panama: Panama will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and the Council’s continued engagement on Somalia, while stressing that the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia must be fully respected. Panama also underscores the need for predictable and sustainable financing for African Union-led peace support operations, for full compliance with international humanitarian law and human rights law, for the protection of civilians, and for safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We encourage the Federal Government of Somalia and the federal member states to work together on security sector reform, reconciliation and inclusive political processes, and we call on all States in the region to resolve disputes peacefully and to refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the United Kingdom for its continued leadership as penholder. We welcome the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and support this resolution. Given the continuing threat posed by Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates, it is essential to avoid security gaps and to ensure a conditions-based, orderly transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. We appreciate that our request concerning the timeline in OP11 was accommodated, and we stress that predictable, sustainable and adequate financing remains critical, including through the timely joint costed proposal and full respect for the budgetary procedures and prerogatives of the General Assembly. We also underscore the importance of compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law, protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and the incorporation of key elements we have consistently advocated, including full and timely implementation of the modalities under resolution 2719 (2023), adequate, predictable and sustainable financing, and a fixed date for the Council’s financing decision. We stress that AUSSOM must implement its mandate in full compliance with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, including the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, protect civilians, facilitate unhindered humanitarian access, and ensure the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women. We also call on the Federal Government of Somalia and the federal member states to cooperate on national priorities, and on all regional States to respect Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity.
before.Somalia:
Mr./Madam President,

Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholder and all Council members for engaging with our core concerns. We particularly welcome the provision in operative paragraph 1, which confirms that the troop- and police-contributing countries and overall composition of AUSSOM shall be determined in close coordination with, and with the consent of, the Federal Government of Somalia, consistent with the bilateral agreements we have concluded. This reflects Somalia’s sovereignty and primary responsibility for our own security.

We also welcome the reaffirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and the draft’s clear conditions-based approach to the progressive transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces.

At the same time, we regret that the text does not yet operationalize access to United Nations assessed contributions of up to 75 per cent under resolution 2719 (2023) with effect from 1 January 2026. Predictable, sustainable and adequate financing remains essential if AUSSOM is to fulfil its mandate against Al-Shabaab. We will continue to engage constructively so that the joint costed proposal and the Council’s decision by 31 May 2026 deliver the financing modalities Somalia and the mission require.

For these reasons, Somalia supports the renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate and votes in favour.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement on a text that renews AUSSOM’s mandate at a critical moment for Somalia and the region. The United Kingdom remains steadfast in supporting Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity. We underscore the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, advancing the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women, and supporting a conditions-based transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. We also stress the need for predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM, including through full implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), and we call on the Federal Government of Somalia and federal member states to work together on national priorities and on all regional states to resolve disputes peacefully and refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge all members to support this resolution.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank the United Kingdom as penholder and all Council members for their constructive work. AUSSOM continues to play a vital role in supporting Somali-led efforts against Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates, and in creating the conditions for the progressive transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. We welcome the conditions-based approach, the strengthened reporting cycle, and the emphasis on compliance, civilian protection, and humanitarian access. We also stress the need for predictable, sustainable, and flexible financing for AUSSOM, including through full and timely implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), burden-sharing among all partners, and respect for the budgetary procedures and prerogatives of the General Assembly. We underscore the importance of respect for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence, and unity, and we call on all regional States to resolve disputes peacefully and refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine Somalia’s sovereignty. The United States remains committed to working with Somalia, the African Union, and all partners to advance peace, security, and stability in Somalia.

after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution. We proceed from the premise that the continuation of an African Union-led peace support operation in Somalia is necessary to prevent a security vacuum and to support Somali efforts against Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates.

We welcome that the text reaffirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity of Somalia and that the composition of AUSSOM is to be determined in close coordination with, and with the consent of, the Federal Government of Somalia. This is particularly important in the current regional context. We oppose any unilateral actions that could undermine Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

At the same time, we stress that AUSSOM must remain an African Union-led mission with a pan-African command-and-control system and must act with full respect for Somali ownership. The transfer of security responsibilities must be realistic, conditions-based and must not create a security vacuum. We also note that financing for such operations requires careful work in the relevant United Nations bodies, with full respect for the budgetary prerogatives of the General Assembly and without automatic or open-ended obligations for the United Nations budget.

The Russian Federation will continue to support the people and Government of Somalia in strengthening their statehood and security. We call on all external actors to respect Somalia’s sovereignty and to refrain from interference in its internal affairs.
after.Sierra Leone:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution just adopted renewing the mandate of the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM). We thank the United Kingdom for its leadership and constructive engagement, and we welcome the unity of the Council on this important question.

We supported this resolution because it responds to the request of the Federal Government of Somalia, reaffirms Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and preserves Somali ownership and consent, including with respect to the composition of AUSSOM and coordination with troop- and police-contributing countries. It also supports a conditions-based and orderly transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces, which is essential to avoid a security vacuum.

Sierra Leone commends the African Union, AUSSOM troop- and police-contributing countries and all partners for their sacrifices in the fight against Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates. We condemn terrorist attacks and express our deep concern at the humanitarian situation in Somalia. We call for safe, timely, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, and for full compliance with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, including the protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel and children. The full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in peace and security efforts must remain central.

We welcome the emphasis on predictable, sustainable and flexible financing for African Union-led peace support operations and on accelerated implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), while respecting the budgetary procedures and prerogatives of the General Assembly. We look forward to the timely joint costed proposal and to the Council’s decision on financing modalities.

Sierra Leone also stresses the importance of cooperation between the Federal Government of Somalia and the federal member states on security, reconciliation, the constitutional process and inclusive elections. We encourage all States in the region to resolve disputes peacefully, to respect Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and to refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine regional stability.

We will continue to support Somalia and the region. Thank you.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia thanks the penholder, the United Kingdom, and all Council members for the adoption of this resolution. The renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate until 31 December 2026 is important for sustaining pressure on Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates and for preventing a security vacuum.

We welcome the Council’s reaffirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and the explicit recognition that the composition of AUSSOM, including troop- and police-contributing countries, must be determined in close coordination with and with the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia, consistent with the bilateral agreements we have concluded. This is a matter of Somali ownership and primary responsibility. All international support must respect Somalia’s consent and must not undermine our national security arrangements or regional stability.

We also welcome the conditions-based approach to the progressive transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces. Somalia remains committed to the Somali Security Development Plan and the National Security Architecture, to building accountable and sustainable security institutions, and to working with the federal member states and our partners. We call for timely, predictable and sustainable financing for AUSSOM in line with resolution 2719 (2023), including accelerated implementation of the African Union–United Nations Roadmap and the hybrid model, so that the mission can deliver its mandate without gaps.

Somalia will continue to work with the African Union, the United Nations, troop- and police-contributing countries and all partners on the basis of full respect for our sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity, and in pursuit of a stable, peaceful and secure Somalia.

Thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United Kingdom warmly welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia. This sends a clear signal of the Council’s continued support for Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and for Somali-led efforts to counter Al-Shabaab and ISIL/Da’esh affiliates.

We thank all Council members for their constructive engagement. The United Kingdom remains committed to working with Somalia, the African Union, troop- and police-contributing countries and international partners to ensure that AUSSOM can implement its mandate effectively, protect civilians, facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and support a conditions-based transfer of security responsibilities to Somali forces.

Predictable and sustainable financing remains essential. We look forward to the timely implementation of resolution 2719 (2023), including the strategic review and reporting requested by this resolution, and to close coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia and the federal member states. We also reiterate the importance of the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in peace and security efforts. The United Kingdom will continue to support Somalia and the region in pursuing peace, security and stability.
